title: Refresh an expiring vSAN Data Protection session token mid-run without repeating completed work
prompt:
Implement `VsanDpProtect/VsanDpProtect.psm1` as a PowerShell 7.4 module for VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1. It drives the vSAN Data Protection snapshot appliance to create a protection group and take one manual protection group snapshot. The appliance issues a short lived session token, and the token this run starts with expires part way through: the module must exchange the credentials for a fresh token and carry on from where it was, without repeating anything the appliance has already done. Creating the protection group a second time is rejected by the appliance, so a restart-from-the-top recovery loses the run.

The environment installs the genuine `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.SddcManager` PowerCLI module version `13.5.0.25380678` and its `VMware.OpenAPI` dependency as prerequisites. The vSAN Data Protection surface has no generated cmdlets in the `VMware.Sdk.Vcf` family, so carry every request over the VMware OpenAPI client those modules ship: build a `VMware.Binding.OpenApi.Client.RequestOptions`, hand it to the caller supplied `VMware.Binding.OpenApi.Client.ApiClient` together with a `VMware.Binding.OpenApi.Client.Configuration` whose `BasePath` is the supplied base path, and read the returned `ApiResponse`. Do not install, download, copy, generate, vendor, intercept, redefine, imitate, or replace VMware modules, assemblies, specifications, harness tools, or their results. Do not bypass the SDK client with `Invoke-WebRequest`, `Invoke-RestMethod`, `System.Net.Http`, `WebClient`, `HttpWebRequest`, curl, wget, raw sockets, or a subprocess. The caller owns the supplied `ApiClient`; do not dispose it.

Read protected `docs/contract.json` and `docs/official_sources.json` first. The focused contract was derived directly from `specifications/vsan-data-protection/vsan-data-protection-openapi.yaml` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at immutable commit `c3f3b52c845dd967cabbc21680e893292077d5ba`; a rendered documentation page is not a contract source. Use exactly the operationIds `Snapservice.Sessions_create`, `Snapservice.Clusters.ProtectionGroups_create$Task`, `Snapservice.Clusters.ProtectionGroups.Snapshots_create$Task`, `Snapservice.Tasks_get`, and `Snapservice.Clusters.ProtectionGroups_list`. Take every method, path template, required query parameter, optional query parameter, request schema, property declaration order and success status from that contract.

Export exactly one function:

`New-VsanDpProtectedSnapshot -ApiClient <VMware.Binding.OpenApi.Client.ApiClient> -BasePath <string> -Credential <pscredential> -ClusterId <string> -ProtectionGroupName <string> -SnapshotName <string> [-VmNamePattern <string[]>] [-VmId <string[]>] [-Locked] [-PolicyName <string>] [-PolicyIntervalUnit <string>] [-PolicyInterval <long>] [-PolicyRetentionUnit <string>] [-PolicyRetentionDuration <long>] [-SnapshotRetentionUnit <string>] [-SnapshotRetentionDuration <long>] [-PollIntervalSeconds <0..60>] [-TimeoutSeconds <1..900>]`

Requirements:

- Reject a null `ApiClient`, a blank `BasePath`, a null `Credential`, a blank `ClusterId`, a blank `ProtectionGroupName` and a blank `SnapshotName` before any request. Require at least one of `VmNamePattern` and `VmId`. The five policy parameters are all-or-nothing, and so are the two snapshot retention parameters. Defaults are `PollIntervalSeconds=2` and `TimeoutSeconds=300`; a zero poll interval must be supported.
- Authenticate with `Snapservice.Sessions_create`. That request carries exactly one `Authorization: Basic <base64 of user:password>` header built from `Credential` and no `vmware-api-session-id` header. Its `201` payload is the bare session token. Every other operation carries exactly one `vmware-api-session-id` header holding the current token and no `Authorization` header. Every request carries exactly one `Accept: application/json` header, and requests with a body carry exactly one `Content-Type: application/json` header.
- Create the protection group with `Snapservice.Clusters.ProtectionGroups_create$Task`, take the `202` task identifier, and poll `Snapservice.Tasks_get` for that exact identifier until it reports `SUCCEEDED`; its `result` is the protection group identifier. `PENDING`, `RUNNING` and `BLOCKED` are nonterminal. Throw `InvalidOperationException` for `FAILED` or an unknown status and `TimeoutException` when the timeout expires. Then request the snapshot with `Snapservice.Clusters.ProtectionGroups.Snapshots_create$Task` against that protection group identifier and poll its task the same way; that `result` is the snapshot identifier. Finally call `Snapservice.Clusters.ProtectionGroups_list` filtered by `pgs` with only the protection group identifier, and require exactly one returned item whose `pg` matches ordinal case-sensitively.
- When any operation answers `401`, do not surface it and do not restart the workflow. Call `Snapservice.Sessions_create` again, adopt the new token, and replay only the request that was rejected; the identifiers, tasks and results already obtained still stand. Refresh at most once per rejected request: a second consecutive `401` for the same request is an `InvalidOperationException`. Never send the expired token again after a refresh, and never call `Snapservice.Sessions_create` when nothing has been rejected.
- Serialize both request bodies as compact JSON with no insignificant whitespace, properties in the order `properties_in_declaration_order` gives them in `docs/contract.json`. Every optional property whose parameter was not supplied must be absent from the payload, not `null`, `false`, `0`, `""` or `[]`: that covers `vm_name_patterns`, `vms` and `tag_rules` inside `Snapservice.TargetEntities`, and `snapshot_policies`, `locked` and `replication_policies` inside `Snapservice.ProtectionGroupSpec`, and `retention` inside `Snapservice.Clusters.ProtectionGroups.Snapshots.CreateSpec`. `locked` appears only when `-Locked` is present. Optional query parameters obey the same rule: send `vmw-task=true` where the contract requires it, send `pgs` on the list call, and send nothing else.
- Return one object with properties exactly in this order: `clusterId`, `protectionGroupId`, `protectionGroupName`, `protectionGroupStatus`, `createTaskId`, `snapshotTaskId`, `snapshotId`, `snapshotName`, `sessionCreateCount`, `tokenRefreshCount`. `protectionGroupName` and `protectionGroupStatus` come from the listed item's `info`. `sessionCreateCount` is how many times `Snapservice.Sessions_create` was called and `tokenRefreshCount` how many of those were refreshes. Write no diagnostic or partial objects to the success pipeline.

Run `python3 -B .protected/verify.py`. The protected verifier creates runtime-only credentials, cluster, protection group, snapshot, task and token identifiers; starts a contract-pinned mock appliance on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port whose only callable routes are derived from the five operationIds in `docs/contract.json`; expires the first session token at a different point in each of its two runs; and reads the mock's flushed and fsynced JSONL request log. It asserts the exact ordered methods, raw targets, header multiplicity and values, body bytes, media types, task identifier continuity across the refresh, that the expired token is never replayed, that the protection group and the snapshot are each accepted exactly once, and that every unset optional field and query parameter is omitted. No live VMware endpoint is contacted. Everything under `.protected/` and `docs/`, plus `VsanDpProtect/VsanDpProtect.psd1`, is protected. Create only `VsanDpProtect/VsanDpProtect.psm1`.
scenario: the session token issued at login expires part way through a protection group create and snapshot workflow, at a different point in each run
constraint: the contract-pinned loopback request log proves the token was refreshed in place, completed work was never repeated, and every unset optional field and query parameter was omitted
